title: Circuit symbols and circuit diagrams practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: Original workshop, greenhouse and test-bench contexts assess mapped symbol recognition and circuit construction patterns without copying official wording, values or diagrams.

questions.prompt: State the electrical quantity measured by (a) an ammeter and (b) a voltmeter.
Which feature distinguishes the symbol for a variable resistor from the symbol for a fixed resistor?

options.A: A diagonal arrow across the resistor
options.C: A long line beside a short line
options.D: The letter V inside the resistor

questions.prompt: A cell, closed switch and lamp are intended to form one working loop. Which description guarantees a complete circuit?

options.A: One terminal of the cell is left unconnected
options.B: The wire crosses itself once without a junction dot
options.C: A continuous path passes through the cell, switch and lamp and returns to the cell
options.D: The lamp is drawn closest to the cell

questions.prompt: A voltmeter is to measure the potential difference across a lamp. How should it be connected?

options.A: In the main path before the cell
options.B: Across the two terminals of the lamp
options.C: Across the two terminals of the ammeter

questions.prompt: A student sketches a circuit for a cell, an open switch, a lamp and a voltmeter intended to measure the potential difference across the lamp.

figure.purpose: Assess circuit-symbol identification and diagnosis of a meter-connection error.

figure.alt_text: A circuit has a cell, an open switch and a lamp in one loop, with a voltmeter incorrectly placed in the same loop.
